title: A list of types
description:
Template metaprogramming treats **types as data**. The basic data structure is a list of types: an empty struct whose only content is its parameter pack.

Using `TypeList` (provided), write three metafunctions. Each takes a list apart with a partial specialization that names the pack.

- `Length<List>::value`: how many types.
- `Contains<T, List>::value`: is `T` one of them? (a fold over `||` with `std::is_same_v`)
- `Front<List>::type`: the first type.
hints: Each metafunction has an undefined (or default) primary template and a partial specialization that opens the list: `template <typename... Ts> struct Length<TypeList<Ts...>> { static constexpr std::size_t value{ sizeof...(Ts) }; };`.
`Contains` folds `(std::is_same_v<T, Ts> || ...)`; `Front` specializes `TypeList<First, Rest...>` and gives `using type = First;`.
